subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should this issue remain the canonical Windows gateway-down umbrella while maintainers split separate fixes for lifecycle recovery, invalid-config repair, browser isolation, pricing readiness, and Claude CLI shim behavior?
rationale: The report combines credible failures across stable gateway, CLI config repair, browser plugin runtime, pricing/provider behavior, and Windows service lifecycle; the safe fix order and recovery UX require maintainer ownership rather than one autonomous patch.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Fixes
options.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow maintainer-owned fixes for each proven sub-boundary.

options.title: Require Live Windows Proof First
options.body: Pause implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures Windows process, listener, browser, and startup timing proof for the highest-risk paths.

options.title: Close Fixed Sub-Branches Later
options.body: After proving main-only hardening ships, close or mark only the resolved sub-areas while leaving remaining failures tracked elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Fixes
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow maintainer-owned fixes for each proven sub-boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest current-history signal across the gateway lifecycle, config guard, pricing, browser launch, Windows restart handoff, and spawn-shim surfaces.
